headline: Kennedy Center to close after judge blocks Trump's name
summary: The board that runs the Kennedy Center in Washington voted Tuesday to close its main building for renovations. Hours earlier, a federal judge ruled again that only Congress can put Trump's name on it. Trump chairs the board. Its resolution cites water damage that caused a partial ceiling collapse. Axios could not confirm when it closes.

cover_question.q: Why can't he just put his name on it?

cover_answer: A judge says only Congress can. Twice now.
table_question: If you pay to fix something, do you get to put your name on it?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The Kennedy Center is a big building in Washington where people go to hear music and see plays. Water got in and part of a ceiling fell, so the people in charge voted to close it and fix it. That's like shutting a classroom while the roof gets patched. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: The name fight means nothing at five. A leaky roof does.

8-12.script: The Kennedy Center's board wanted Trump's name on the building. A judge said no, twice: only Congress can change the name. Hours later the board, which Trump chairs, voted to close it for repairs. A referee's call: argue all you want, the rulebook isn't yours.
8-12.why: A rule, a ruling, and a reaction, in that order.

13-17.script: Is the Kennedy Center closing for safety or for leverage? The board says water damage collapsed part of a ceiling. Its own filing also says Trump is unlikely to oversee the renovation without his name on the building. Which reason would you put first?
13-17.why: Two stated reasons, one decision. Let them weigh it.

5-7.a: The big building is closing to get fixed. The plan is to move the big shows to other places for a while. The grown-ups have it.

8-12.q: Why can't he just put his name on it?
8-12.a: A judge says only Congress can change the name. The board tried in August, and the same judge had already said no in May.

8-12.q: Is the building really falling apart?
8-12.a: The board's resolution says water got in and part of a ceiling collapsed. Axios says the renovation would fix corrosion and the theaters.

13-17.q: Is closing it a safety call or a pressure move?
13-17.a: The board says safety and cites the ceiling. Its filing also says Trump is unlikely to oversee the renovation without his name on it. Read both.
Axios cites a Washington Post report that ticket sales plunged after the board voted to name the center after Trump.
